results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 76 aligned draft units summarize to the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (e.g. p24 'Generic models: listing is a publication about a property', p53 'Essen Golf: late removal becomes one context's problem'); the five introduction callouts match no spec paragraph and are callouts by design.

Outliner marked p13, p31, p46, p67 (and the KEY POINTS callout). p13 joins two tactical terms announced as a pair ('Two more terms come from DDD's tactical design'); p31's partnership clause names the trust-catalog relationship, which is the paragraph's point on the map; p67 frames no-owner explicitly as split ownership's 'mirror image'; the KEY POINTS callout is the three-part thesis statement by design. These pass; p46 is a separate result.

results.quote: The models' numbers make the one-owner pattern concrete. In the general model, the listing is owned by one capability and read by eleven others, and two more query it through search.
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases ('Models show one owner, many readers / ownership assignments need review too'). The second idea, the cookie-consent mis-assignment, is about non-listing data and does not develop the first; the spec's own controlling idea for p46 joins the two with 'and', so the draft follows the spec faithfully.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: scene and concepts set up S1; subdomains and vertical differences support S5 (per-brand classification); One Listing, Many Models supports S1/S3; the context map S4; aggregates and the listing event S3; the worked example and public record S5; trade-offs, failure modes, Chief Architect's view and questions apply S3-S5; the conclusion synthesizes the thesis.

All ten tables and four figures are introduced by a lead sentence and read in the prose (e.g. the Owns column in p22, Figure 2 in p25/p51); quotations from Evans, Vernon, Fowler, Conway, Vinted, Kleinanzeigen and Adevinta are each followed by what they show; the Kleinanzeigen inference is labelled as inference.

results.quote: The book also draws on two generic domain models, one for a general-listings marketplace and one for a real-estate marketplace, which are the author's working models and describe no company. They reach the same structure by a different route.
results.finding: Declared similarity carrying 'the structure Veldmark's contexts show', placed at the start of p24. The opening sentence is additive ('also draws on') and introduces a new source; the similarity comes only in the second sentence and never names the structure it is 'the same' as (one owner, many readers in the Lyon table), so the boundary from p23 is weakly marked. Flow reader A also found the models 'arrive abruptly after the Lyon discussion'.

results.quote: The context map's skeleton is shared across verticals. What changes is which contexts exist, which are core and where the entity sits.
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying 'Decisions that apply to every marketplace' (the three trade-offs just made) into what differs by vertical. The opening picks up the context map, not the trade-offs, so the step from Trade-offs is unmarked; both flow readers said the section's placement is only partly clear.

All other transition_in entries (69 boundaries) express their declared relationship at the start of the unit, e.g. p25 'Meanings with owners still need rules for how they talk' (cause_effect), p36 'Bounded contexts set the boundaries of models. Aggregates set the boundaries of transactions inside them' (elaboration), p47 'The sections so far showed the finished map...' (elaboration), p69 'Those failures come from owners and relationships nobody decided' (cause_effect); the failure-mode and trade-off units are parallel items announced by their lead-ins. The hand-off link to vertical-requirements is present.

Flow-A item 1: 'Leaving the reason for later forces the reader to carry an open puzzle through five sections. I re-read the sentence to check whether I had missed an explanation.' The order is the spec's and is fine; the draft adds a forward reference to a numbered step three sections away, in an overloaded three-clause sentence, when it could state the reason (French prices include agency fees) or drop the pointer.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3 item 1 ('"Step 2" points to a numbered list that the reader has not seen yet ... I had to re-read it.')

results.quote: Even their mistakes make the case for named owners: the general model's data catalog assigns credentials, sessions and the audit log to the cookie-consent capability, a reminder that ownership assignments must be reviewed as carefully as boundaries.
results.finding: Flow-A item 2: 'this paragraph felt like an aside ... the cookie-consent point to see how it bears on listings. It does not.' The draft already adds the linking phrase the round-4 judge asked for, and readers in rounds 3, 4 and 5 still stumble; the difficulty comes from the spec placing a mistake about non-listing data in the section on listing meanings, so the fault is the spec (cut the mistake or move it to the Chief Architect's watch list).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3 item 4 ('This is a side remark about an error in the author's own working model ... it pulls attention away from the point of the section.')

results.quote: Hearthly's events reach the group event backbone through a bridge from Google Pub/Sub.
results.finding: Flow-A: 'This sentence ends a paragraph about the catalog as an open host service and has nothing to do with that point. It is explained only later, in Step 4.' The spec asks for the bridge in p28; the draft appends it as a bare infrastructure fact instead of tying it to the published language (for example: every brand's events, Hearthly's through a bridge, reach the backbone in this one language).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3 item 5 ('This is out of place ... It makes sense only in Step 4 of the worked example.')

results.quote: As Chief Architect, these are the decisions I would keep at group level, and the ones I would leave to brands.
results.finding: Flow-A: 'The switch to first person is abrupt, because the story already has a Group Chief Architect (Ingrid). For a moment I was unsure whether "I" was Ingrid or the author.' The spec wants the author's view; the draft does not mark that 'I' is the author rather than Veldmark's Group Chief Architect.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3 item 9 ('For a moment I was unsure whether "I" meant the author or Ingrid.')

results.quote: The context map's skeleton is shared across verticals. What changes is which contexts exist, which are core and where the entity sits.
results.finding: Flow-A, section 2: 'Partly clear ... nothing in particular puts it between Trade-offs and Failure Modes rather than elsewhere.' The spec's position is defensible (contrast with decisions that apply to every marketplace) and both readers call it acceptable, but the prose never states why the section comes here; a bridge from the trade-offs would fix it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 2 'Vertical Differences' ('the reason is only partly clear. It does not build on the trade-offs ... reads as a short aside')

results.quote: That is the same idea from the other side: a stable language at the boundary lets the model behind it change.
results.finding: Flow-A: 'I had to re-read to work out which "side" was meant.' Not reported by flow-B.

results.quote: At Motorvane, where 91% of supply comes from about 21,400 dealers verified at contract signature, most of it by feed, it is supporting.
results.finding: Flow-A: 'I paused to reconcile the two percentages' (91% here vs 88% of dealer listings by feed in the scene); they measure different things but the text does not say so. Not reported by flow-B.

results.finding: Flow-B item 2: 'the table and the paragraphs after it never use core, supporting or generic. The link between the two sections is claimed rather than shown.' Not reported by flow-A (who found the order clear).

results.finding: Flow-B item 10: the reference models were last mentioned several sections earlier and their 'resilience analysis' was never introduced; B had to look back. Not reported by flow-A.

Domain-driven design terms are defined before use in Concepts; DMS is expanded at first use; terms on the journal's does_not_know list that appear (liquidity, VIN) were introduced in earlier chapters of the book (business-capabilities and the Veldmark chapters it links to). Valuo and 'resilience analysis' are recorded as one-reader flow findings; neither is a technical term the audience lacks.

The opening bridges from the previous chapter's capability map to a decomposition question, then hooks with the overloaded noun (six correct answers) and states the thesis in KEY POINTS; it is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary, dawn-of-man or book report.
The closing answers the forum's question, states the consequence and a course of action, and hands off; no 'in conclusion' opener, no new idea, no body evidence, not only a rephrased thesis.

p76 synthesizes ('six models, joined by an identifier and the published listing event ... one context decides') and answers so-what ('The Essen Golf's late removal becomes one context's freshness contract instead of a bug in six places, and a brand can change its ranking or its packages without a cross-team project').
p76 opens 'The forum's question, *what is a listing, and who decides?*, now has an answer in two halves' and returns to the six people, matching the declared callback.

The cold reader of the opening predicted the sections in the declared order (six answers; terms; subdomains; one listing through ten contexts; context map and relationships; aggregates; listing event; Veldmark's map; public record; trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, review questions) and the evidence (fictional Veldmark, DDD terms, public engineering sources, tables and a context-map diagram), matching AC-2's expected answer. Its side note (six meanings vs ten contexts) is not a prediction failure.

The reader answered that the catalog decides; ingestion translates the feed removal into a Withdraw command; the catalog emits ListingRemoved on Listing event contract v1; search, alerts and leads consume it within their deadlines and never write state back; the 26-hour feed delay stays ingestion's freshness contract with the dealer. Matches expected.

The reader classified trust and safety per brand: core at the classifieds brand (C2C scams), supporting at the dealer-heavy car brand (verified at contract); a group platform shares the pipeline with policies configurable per brand and country, and core contexts stay with the brand even when the engine is shared. Matches expected.

The reader explained that the one transaction crosses aggregates in two contexts (entitlement account in monetization, listing in the catalog); monetization grants the entitlement keyed by order ID, sends ApplyPlacement and publishes VisibilityChanged, retries reuse the key; if the listing was removed the catalog rejects the command and monetization refunds or re-credits; atomic within each aggregate, eventual between. Matches expected.
